issues.quote: the `wrong-total` run already prints one, order 1 cut to its keyboard line, showing 0: that one-line case is your smallest reproduction. In the sample data order 2 has that shape, one line; order 3 has two, which is how the template's worked example below numbers them.
issues.text: I read this twice. The printed one-line case is 'order 1 cut', yet the next sentence brings in orders 2 and 3 and points ahead to an example I have not seen. I worked it out (order 2 is a real order of the same shape) but only on the second pass.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: first 'The run's one-line case, order 1 cut to its keyboard line, shows 0: that is your smallest reproduction.' then 'In the sample data, order 2 is a real order of that shape; the worked example below cites it by number.'

issues.quote: in the sample data half the orders have several lines and come out short, the other half show 0, so every order is wrong
issues.text: The lesson only ever names orders 1, 2 and 3, two multi-line and one single-line, so 'half' does not match what I was shown. I paused to wonder whether there are more orders. The conclusion 'every order is wrong' still follows either way.
issues.fix: Add a clause saying how many orders the sample data holds (e.g. 'of its N orders, half have several lines'), or drop 'half' and say 'multi-line orders come out short, one-line orders show 0, so every order is wrong'.

issues.quote: `Bằng chứng` names orders by number, one of them the smallest case that still fails.
issues.text: The smallest case I actually ran has no order number (it is order 1 cut). To name one by number I must cite order 2 from the worked example, which I never ran. I can do it, but I was unsure whether evidence I did not produce myself counts.
issues.fix: Add to step 1 one clause: 'for Bằng chứng, you may cite order 2 as the worked example does, since it has the same one-line shape as the case the run prints.'

issues.quote: An impact line reading "every customer with an order, every order in the sample data, no way around it" covers what `Mức ảnh hưởng` asks.
issues.text: The lesson says the field asks 'how many of them', meaning people. The option's 'how many' part counts orders, not people, so I hesitated before ticking it as covering the field.
issues.fix: Change the middle part to a count of people, e.g. 'every customer with an order, all of them, no way around it', or make the lesson's gloss read 'how many (people or records)'.
